original_question: Let G be a graph homeomorphic to the Petersen graph. If each path in G made of two successive segments is a geodesic, each cycle of G containing five segments has odd length, and all cycles of G containing six segments have equal length, are these three conditions not only sufficient but also necessary for G to be geodetic?
target_in_paper: Section A, "Open Problems Related to Characterization" (page 8): the Petersen-graph instance of the unnumbered conjecture that the three listed sufficient conditions for a graph homeomorphic to the Petersen graph are also necessary for geodeticity. The note explicitly says that the three conditions in the Petersen-graph statement are conjectured to be not only sufficient but also necessary, citing [6].
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right object (a graph homeomorphic to the Petersen graph), the right three hypotheses, and the right unresolved issue in the paper: whether those hypotheses are not merely sufficient but also necessary for geodeticity.
missing_details: The paper's meaning of homeomorphic should be made explicit: two graphs are homeomorphic if they can be obtained by inserting vertices on edges; equivalently here, G is obtained from the Petersen graph by subdividing edges.
The paper uses the notion of a node: a vertex of degree at least 3.
The paper's term segment should be defined: a path whose only nodes are its endpoints.
Geodesic should be defined explicitly as a shortest path between its endpoints.
Geodetic should be defined explicitly: every pair of distinct vertices is joined by a unique geodesic.
The paper measures path and cycle length by number of edges; this should be stated because conditions (ii) and (iii) are metric.
For full faithfulness to the cited source [6], the cycle conditions are sharpened to cycles containing exactly five segments and exactly six segments.
The quantifier should be explicit: the question is whether for every graph G homeomorphic to the Petersen graph, these three conditions characterize geodeticity.
refined_question: Let G be a graph homeomorphic to the Petersen graph, meaning that G is obtained from the Petersen graph by subdividing edges. Call a vertex of degree at least 3 a node, and call a segment a path whose only nodes are its endpoints. A geodesic is a shortest path, and G is geodetic if every pair of distinct vertices is joined by a unique geodesic. Is it true that G is geodetic if and only if (i) every path consisting of two successive segments is a geodesic in G, (ii) every cycle containing exactly five segments has odd length, and (iii) all cycles containing exactly six segments have the same length, where path and cycle length are measured by number of edges?
justification: The draft is very close to the paper's actual intent. In Section A, the note first states the three Petersen-graph conditions as sufficient for geodeticity and then immediately conjectures that the conditions in that statement are also necessary. To make the question stand-alone, one must import the definitions of path, cycle, geodesic, and geodetic from Section A, and the definitions of node, segment, and homeomorphic graph from Section B. The sharper wording with exactly five and exactly six segments comes from the source [6] that the note cites for this conjectural characterization.
